note: Files this project's cleaners were ported from. scripts/check-upstream.mjs compares the live content against these hashes; when one moves, re-port the mirror files listed under `mirrors` and update `sha256` in the same commit.
followUp: tests/golden/imageMeta.json and tests/golden/layerA.json hold values generated from `unmark-web`, never from this project's own TypeScript: goldens produced by the code under test assert nothing. If either unmark-web source changed, regenerate as part of the re-port with `npm run regen:golden` (needs a local unmark-web checkout; see UNMARK_WEB_DIR in scripts/regen-golden.mjs), otherwise the tests keep asserting the old behaviour and the drift ships anyway.

sources.comment: Deliberately partial mirror: upstream added BMP, GIF and TIFF in guillaumemeyer/watermarks-remover#107 and unmark-web ports all three, but only GIF is mirrored here — it is the only one of the three that gets uploaded to WordPress in practice. A green check on this source therefore means 'no change we decided to track', not 'byte-for-byte feature parity'. If BMP or TIFF ever matter here, port stripBmp/stripTiff from unmark-web's js/image_meta.js. The ISOBMFF primitives this module exports since unmark-web v0.4.0, and the inspectIsobmff byteScan option added with them, are now mirrored here and used by src/utils/avMeta.ts. byteScan defaults to the previous behaviour, so the image goldens regenerate byte-identical. Upstream #264 is mirrored in full: the C2PA ContentProvenanceBox user type d8fec3d6-1b0e-483c-9297-5828877ec481 is recognized and stripped in inspectIsobmff and stripIsobmff, so AVIF/HEIC and, through avMeta.ts, MP4/MOV now lose a manifest whose payload carries no ASCII c2pa/jumb marker. Upstream #261 is not mirrored and needs no counterpart: it makes clean_image's post-clean scan skip an exiftool subprocess and a redundant SynthID call, neither of which exists here. watermarks-remover#308 is mirrored in full: a zTXt/iTXt value that inflates past MAX_PNG_TEXT_DECOMPRESSED_BYTES (1 MiB) is refused rather than allocated, inspectPng reports the chunk as not fully inspected and stripPng drops it even in keep mode. The same change swapped zlib.decompress for a decompressobj, so a stream that stops early now yields the prefix it decoded instead of nothing; the inflate here does the same, and keeps returning null for a stream that is corrupt rather than merely short.

Full mirror, both drivers: the buffer driver the golden file pins byte for byte, and the slice driver that walks box and chunk headers through File.slice() so a video is cleaned without being held. Unlike the image port there is no deliberate format gap here; every container unmark-web handles (MP4/MOV/M4A/M4V, WAV, MP3, FLAC) is handled here. Since unmark-web's #264 sync it also carries containsC2paProvBoxInFile, the chunked counterpart of the whole-file user-type scan that the slice driver needs because it disables the per-box one. watermarks-remover#201 is mirrored in full: an ID3v2 tag whose declared size overruns the file is reported as truncated instead of silently parsing to nothing, and a clean drops it up to the first valid MPEG frame header, or preserves the file when there is no such header to find. Both drivers carry it, and the slice driver scans for the frame header in chunks rather than reading the file.

Also partial in a second way since watermarks-remover#156: that change hardened the error handling around the external c2patool subprocess, which has no counterpart in a browser or in this converter. Partial in a third way since watermarks-remover 8e16b822, which passes creationflags=subprocess_creationflags to every subprocess.run so a child process opens no console window on Windows: neither a browser nor this converter starts child processes. Partial in two more ways since 2026-08-27: upstream #252 refuses HTTP redirects in _synthid_score_http to block SSRF, and #254 adds a `changed` field to clean_image's returned dict for clean_file.py's new --only-changed flag. Neither has a counterpart here: this converter makes no HTTP calls, and clean() returns bytes rather than writing a file, so the caller already holds both sides to compare. Upstream #264 is mirrored in full: the C2PA ContentProvenanceBox user type d8fec3d6-1b0e-483c-9297-5828877ec481 is recognized and stripped in inspectIsobmff and stripIsobmff, so AVIF/HEIC and, through avMeta.ts, MP4/MOV now lose a manifest whose payload carries no ASCII c2pa/jumb marker. Upstream #261 is not mirrored and needs no counterpart: it makes clean_image's post-clean scan skip an exiftool subprocess and a redundant SynthID call, neither of which exists here. watermarks-remover#308 is mirrored in full: a zTXt/iTXt value that inflates past MAX_PNG_TEXT_DECOMPRESSED_BYTES (1 MiB) is refused rather than allocated, inspectPng reports the chunk as not fully inspected and stripPng drops it even in keep mode. The same change swapped zlib.decompress for a decompressobj, so a stream that stops early now yields the prefix it decoded instead of nothing; the inflate here does the same, and keeps returning null for a stream that is corrupt rather than merely short. Three more changes since 2026-09-01 have no counterpart here and are not mirrored: #302 renamed the CtrlRegen and DiffusionPurification `strength` parameters to `intensity` (subprocess flags for pixel-domain removers this converter cannot run), #201 added synthid_is_watermarked and a SynthID verdict finding to inspect_image (needs a scorer this port does not have), and run_synthid_score gained a `data` parameter to skip a read-back that never happens here.

Root source. Changes here land in unmark-web first; this entry catches the window before that happens. watermarks-remover#201 is mirrored in full: an ID3v2 tag whose declared size overruns the file is reported as truncated instead of silently parsing to nothing, and a clean drops it up to the first valid MPEG frame header, or preserves the file when there is no such header to find. Both drivers carry it, and the slice driver scans for the frame header in chunks rather than reading the file. Partial in one way: inspect_av and clean_av take filesystem paths and use safe_write_bytes, and clean_av re-inspects what it wrote, none of which has a counterpart in a browser. The reporting that re-inspection feeds, including inspection_incomplete, is mirrored. Partial in one more way since upstream #254: clean_av's returned dict gained a `changed` field for clean_file.py's new --only-changed flag. cleanAv here returns the bytes rather than writing a file, so the caller already holds both sides to compare. Partial in one more way since the #201 sync: inspect_av gained a `data` parameter so an HTTP caller can skip a read-back, which a caller that already holds the bytes has no use for.
